clue.text: What we can't look back on if we use the Channel tunnel

definitions.text: What we can't look back on if we use the Channel tunnel

parts.words: What we can't look back on if we use the Channel tunnel
parts.note: ferry passengers leaving England see the famous chalk coastline of Kent recede behind them; a train underground under the sea shows nothing

explanation.surface: A wistful complaint that rail travellers to France miss a classic farewell view.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 18 Down to make the full name of the Kent landmark; 'look back on' is literal, glancing behind from a departing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The chalk cliffs near the port in Kent are the traditional last sight of England for sea passengers.

clue.text: Last place ambitious soccer teams want to get to

definitions.text: Last place ambitious soccer teams want to get to

parts.words: Last place ambitious soccer teams want to get to
parts.note: 'last place' sounds like the bottom of a league table, but means the venue of the final, the English cup final stadium

explanation.surface: A remark about football clubs dreading finishing at the bottom of the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last place' looks like relegation, which no ambitious team wants; it is the stadium in London where the FA Cup final, the last match, is played.
explanation.definitionFit: The national stadium in north-west London hosts English football's cup finals, the goal of every cup run.

clue.text: Rail union that is about to get accustomed to hardships

indicators.note: about here means going around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is' (id est)
NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, the British rail workers' union

explanation.surface: Railway workers' union officials are about to toughen up for difficult times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals enclosure; 'Rail' suggests track, but it is the old British railwaymen's union. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To harden someone or oneself so that suffering no longer troubles them is the verb's meaning.

clue.text: One who aims to go far in politics

definitions.text: One who aims to go far in politics

parts.words: One who aims to go far in politics
parts.note: 'go far' suggests career ambition, but here it means holding views far from the centre

explanation.surface: A description of an ambitious young politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A person holding far-left or far-right opinions has gone to the furthest point of the political spectrum.

clue.text: Rackets may put them up in court

definitions.text: Rackets may put them up in court

parts.words: Rackets may put them up in court
parts.note: suggests crooked schemes bringing people before a judge, but means tennis rackets hitting high balls on a tennis court

explanation.surface: Criminal enterprises landing people in front of a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: High looping shots in tennis are hit up into the air by a racket on the court.

clue.text: Raise money in the stock market to test public opinion

definitions.text: Raise money in the stock market
definitions.meaning: an old financial idiom for raising credit through accommodation bills
to float an idea to see how people react

explanation.surface: A financier's two strategies: raising capital and sounding out the public.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom both for obtaining credit with accommodation bills and for floating a trial proposal to gauge reaction.

clue.text: Play for time to accommodate an ox, maybe

definitions.meaning: a compartment in a cowshed or stable housing one animal

explanation.surface: A farmer dithering over where to house an ox.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both delaying tactics and a single animal's compartment in a byre or stable.

clue.text: A bit of mark? Yes

parts.note: 'mark' looks like a stain or a scratch; here it is the old German currency, and the coin was its smallest part, a hundredth

explanation.surface: A quick question and answer about a small stain or blemish.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Mark' is the Deutschmark, not a blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: The small German coin was one hundredth of the Deutschmark before the euro.

clue.text: Naturally it's particularly slow to get up to the centre

indicators.note: 'to the centre' tells us the second 'to' goes into the middle of the other phrase

parts.note: to get up means to rise, written as the two words to rise

explanation.surface: Something that by its nature is very slow to climb to the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the centre' places TO in the middle of TO RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: The shelled reptile is proverbially the slowest of animals, as in the fable with the hare.

clue.text: Gets on a reddish-brown horse on the Cornish coast

parts.note: to get on a horse is to mount it
a bay is a horse with a reddish-brown coat

explanation.surface: A rider climbing onto a chestnut-coloured horse beside the sea in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Mount's Bay is the wide bay in west Cornwall overlooked by St Michael's Mount.
explanation.definitionFit: The bay facing St Michael's Mount lies on Cornwall's southern shore near Penzance.

clue.text: Of a mind to make amends

definitions.meaning: in agreement, read as the two words ...
to make up for a wrong

explanation.surface: Someone resolved to make up for what they did.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means in agreement; as one, to expiate a wrong.

clue.text: Badly riled about East German songs

indicators.note: about means the rearranged word goes round the other piece
badly signals that the letters of riled are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: Someone irritated by songs from East Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges RILED to LIDER; 'about' puts it round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are the art songs of the Romantic German repertoire, by Schubert or Schumann.

clue.text: Not wanted at the feast, hide him in the cupboard!

definitions.text: Not wanted at the feast, hide him in the cupboard!

parts.words: Not wanted at the feast, hide him in the cupboard!
parts.note: points to the '... at the feast' (a gloomy guest) and the '... in the cupboard' (a hidden scandal)

explanation.surface: A host desperate to hide an unwelcome guest from the dinner party.
explanation.walkthrough: Two idioms: a spectre at the feast spoils the fun, and a family secret is hidden in the cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Both idioms use the bony frame: a gloomy presence at a celebration and a secret kept from view.

clue.text: Classical historian reflecting about return of Old English in Somerset

indicators.note: about means the turned name goes round the other piece
reflecting means the historian's name is seen in a mirror, back to front

parts.note: Livy was the Roman historian of early Rome

indicators.note: return of means the letters for Old English are turned back

explanation.surface: A Roman historian musing about the revival of Anglo-Saxon in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflecting' turns the historian round to YVIL; 'return of' turns the Old English abbreviation, which 'about' places within. Yeovil is a Somerset town.
explanation.definitionFit: The market town is in south Somerset, so the definition places it in that county.

clue.text: The converse of young boys who shared the same teachers

definitions.text: The converse of young boys who shared the same teachers

parts.words: The converse of young boys who shared the same teachers
parts.note: old boys are former pupils of a school; swap both words for their opposites to get former female pupils

explanation.surface: A description of schoolboys who sat in the same classrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old boys' are a school's former male pupils; flip 'old' to 'young' and 'girls' to 'boys' and you get the clue's phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Former female pupils of one school form its alumnae association, the counterpart of old boys.

clue.text: Not in a seat, but hoping to get one possibly

definitions.meaning: on one's feet rather than sitting
a candidate ... for a parliamentary seat

explanation.surface: A commuter stuck on their feet, hoping for somewhere to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is British election usage: a candidate 'stands' for a seat in Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means upright, not sitting, and also being an election candidate for a constituency.

clue.text: An apple of unrivalled excellence

definitions.meaning: an old variety of dessert apple

explanation.surface: Praise for the finest apple there is.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word means without equal, and is also the name of an old apple variety.

clue.text: Government publication that might be kept under the librarian'scounter!

definitions.text: Government publication that might be kept under the librarian'scounter!

parts.words: Government publication that might be kept under the librarian'scounter!
parts.note: an official parliamentary report has the same name as a racy, risqué book that a librarian might hide from view

explanation.surface: A dull official report that a librarian keeps hidden away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' also means smutty, so an official report shares its name with a book a prim librarian would keep under the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Official British parliamentary reports were bound in blue covers, and 'blue' also means indecent.

clue.text: Unfashionable way in which Dolly set out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of Dolly and set are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A woman named Dolly dressed in a dated manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DOLLY SET; 'in which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dated or old-fashioned is in a manner belonging to the past.

clue.text: See 1

annotationWithheld.why: See 1: this light is the second half of the linked answer to 1 Across, whose clue is a cryptic definition of the whole name; the puzzle file carries no group link, so the whole is annotated on 1 Across

clue.text: A wild glen with a girl's name

indicators.note: wild signals that the letters of glen are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A remote Scottish valley that happens to carry a woman's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' scrambles the valley word, which sits between the two single letters given by 'A' and 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common female first name, as borne by the German chancellor Merkel.

clue.text: Opposed to profit in a way

indicators.note: in means the profit is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a profit is a gain

explanation.surface: Someone who objects to making money in a certain manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something means being in opposition to it.

clue.text: Thirsty fellows ringing first, rate milk suppliers

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the dry letters go round the other piece

parts.note: a thirsty person is dry
first-rate is A1, the 1 written as the letter I
fellows means men

explanation.surface: Thirsty men phoning first, then rating the people who supply milk.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a British idiom for first-rate, with the digit read as a letter I; 'ringing' signals enclosure, and the comma is surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Dairy workers produce and deliver milk from the farm.

clue.text: Still around as a cause of ferment

indicators.note: around means the word for still goes around the other word

parts.note: still in the sense 'nevertheless' means yet

explanation.surface: Something that remains active as the source of fermentation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adjective (motionless) but works as the adverb meaning nevertheless; 'around' signals enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: The fungus converts sugar into alcohol and carbon dioxide, driving fermentation in brewing and baking.

clue.text: Parental couple taken round an international waterway

indicators.note: taken round means the parents' letters enclose the next word

parts.note: the two parents, father and mother, are pa and ma
the second parent, mother, is ma

explanation.surface: Mum and Dad on a cruise through a famous canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken round' signals the parents enclosing the next word; the definition leans on the canal, which is what makes the country's name a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: The canal across the Central American isthmus links Atlantic and Pacific and carries ships of every nation.

clue.text: Surrounded by mango chutney

indicators.note: a chutney is fruit chopped and mixed up, so the letters of mango are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something served in the middle of a pot of mango relish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chutney' rearranges MANGO.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the midst of things is to be surrounded by them.

clue.text: Records that may finish up on the fire

definitions.meaning: written records of a voyage or of events

definitions.text: may finish up on the fire
definitions.meaning: pieces of chopped wood for burning

explanation.surface: Old records that end up being burnt.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a ship's or computer's record of events and chunks of firewood.

clue.text: Country house not well placed in Virginia

indicators.note: placed in means the word for not well goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
not well means ill

explanation.surface: A rural mansion badly sited in Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed in' signals insertion; 'well' looks like a water source but pairs with 'not' to mean unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A large country residence, especially a Roman or Italian one, is a villa.

clue.text: It could be now no-one's out on a limb

indicators.note: it could be suggests the letters of now and no-one's might be rearranged to give something else

explanation.surface: A remark that at this point nobody else is isolated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It could be' rearranges NOW NOONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out on a limb means being isolated without support, alone.

clue.text: Makes a fearful departure in a plane

explanation.surface: A nervous traveller leaving by air.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means fleeing in fear and, literally, starting a journey by air.
